smell: Every curl call uses -sSfL but none specify --max-time or --connect-timeout. A hung GitHub API endpoint, release CDN, or sigstore endpoint stalls the installer indefinitely without an interrupt — set -euo pipefail does nothing for an open TCP socket that never returns bytes.
evidence:
curl -sSfL -o "$TMP/$ARCHIVE_NAME" "$ARCHIVE_URL" ||
    die "failed to download $ARCHIVE_URL"

curl -sSfL "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" |
    sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' |
    head -1
fix_summary: Add `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` to every curl invocation in install.sh. For the latest-release lookup keep the timeout shorter (e.g. --max-time 30). Optionally factor a `curl_safe()` helper that wires the standard flags + tries 2 retries with `--retry 2 --retry-connrefused`.
must_preserve: -sSfL set, the cosign cert-identity-regexp, the sha256 verify flow, and the INSECURE skip semantics.

smell: The cosign verify-blob branch is nested inside `if [ -z "$INSECURE" ] && [ -n "$SHA_CMD" ]`, so setting INSECURE=1 disables BOTH sha256 verification AND cosign signature verification. A user who lacks `sha256sum` (uncommon) or wants to skip the checksum dependency for some reason loses the stronger sigstore guarantee as a side effect — even though cosign is independent of sha256sum.
evidence:
if [ -z "$INSECURE" ] && [ -n "$SHA_CMD" ]; then
    info "downloading SHA256SUMS"
    ...
    if command -v cosign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        info "verifying cosign signature on SHA256SUMS"
        ...
fix_summary: Hoist the cosign verify-blob block out of the `INSECURE` conditional so cosign always runs when the binary is present. Keep the sha256-only block guarded by INSECURE — they are independent integrity layers. The current nesting also conflicts with the on-screen INSECURE warning which says "SHA256 and cosign signature verification SKIPPED" — that is currently true, but the design choice is overly broad.
must_preserve: The cosign verify-blob certificate-identity-regexp pin to https://github.com/qxtaiba/okdctl/ and the OIDC-issuer pin to GitHub Actions.

smell: Resolving the latest release tag uses an unauthenticated GitHub API call. GitHub limits unauthenticated API access to 60 requests per hour per IP. CI runners (especially shared-IP cloud build farms) will hit this limit and the installer will fail with a confusing curl error. Pinning VERSION sidesteps the issue but undocumented in the on-screen output when the resolution fails.
evidence:
VERSION=$(curl -sSfL "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/releases/latest" |
    sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' |
    head -1)
[ -n "$VERSION" ] || die "failed to resolve latest release from GitHub API"
fix_summary: When VERSION is unset, allow `GITHUB_TOKEN` if present in env: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" ...` to lift the cap to 5000/hr. Surface a clearer error on rate-limit response (HTTP 403 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0) — `die "GitHub API rate-limited; pin VERSION=v0.x.y or set GITHUB_TOKEN"`.

smell: curl invocations do not use `--proto '=https'` or `--tlsv1.2`. The URLs are hardcoded HTTPS so a downgrade attack would also require a host-header rewrite, but defense-in-depth on a sudo-tier installer that processes a release tarball is cheap.
fix_summary: Add `--proto '=https' --tlsv1.2` to the standard curl flags (e.g. via a `curl_safe()` helper alongside the timeout fix). Pairs naturally with the curl-no-timeout finding.

smell: The `dynamic "disk"` block for the Ceph data disk on master and worker VMs is gated on `var.master_data_disk_size_gb > 0` / `var.worker_data_disk_size_gb > 0`. Lowering either to 0 in a re-apply silently strips the data-disk block from the VM. Because the disk is inside a `dynamic` block, no `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` can attach to it. A typo in tfvars during re-apply is a destructive path with no plan-time warning beyond "-1 disk".
evidence:
dynamic "disk" {
  for_each = var.worker_data_disk_size_gb > 0 ? [1] : []
  content {
    datastore_id = var.data_storage
    size         = var.worker_data_disk_size_gb
    interface    = "scsi1"
    ...
fix_summary: Add a `lifecycle { precondition { ... } }` to the parent VM resource that fails the plan when `var.<role>_data_disk_size_gb` transitions from >0 to 0 — but Terraform preconditions evaluate against current vars only, so the cleaner fix is README documentation plus a tfvars-level guard in the wizard / okdctl Go layer (the latter is in the audit-state-and-recovery seam). At the HCL level, replace `> 0` with `>= var.minimum_data_disk_size_gb` (default 0) and document the destructive-shrink path in the variable description.
must_preserve: The dynamic-disk pattern itself (it is the right way to express "optional disk" in HCL).

smell: All three VM resources `ignore_changes = [network_device, ...]`. Once a VM exists, drift on `var.bridge` or VLAN tag becomes invisible to `terraform plan`. The reason (bpg/proxmox dynamic-block diff confusion when network_device + dynamic network_device coexist) is real but unannotated — a future maintainer auditing the lifecycle block has no way to know the rationale, and may delete the entry assuming it is leftover scaffolding.
fix_summary: Add a one-line comment above `network_device,` in each ignore_changes block explaining the bpg/proxmox dynamic-block diff quirk — same shape as the existing `efi_disk` rationale comment. Without context, an auditor or a future Terraform upgrade reviewer cannot tell which entries are still load-bearing.
must_preserve: The ignore_changes list itself — removing entries triggers spurious replacements.

smell: Master VMs run the etcd quorum for the OKD cluster. There is no `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` (or a `prevent_destroy = var.production` toggle) on `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.master`. A `terraform destroy` from the wrong workspace or an accidental `-target` removes etcd nodes irreversibly. Per seams.md §5 destroy safety is owned by audit-state-and-recovery — but the HCL-idiom-level guard is `prevent_destroy`, which this module does not use.
fix_summary: Add an opt-in `var.protect_masters` (default false to preserve current ergonomics for `okdctl destroy` flows) and gate `prevent_destroy = var.protect_masters` on the master resource's lifecycle. NOTE: prevent_destroy must be a literal boolean — gating on a variable is currently a Terraform limitation. Alternative: document in README that production deployments should add a tfvars-driven override module that wraps with `prevent_destroy = true`. Real fix lives at the okdctl-Go layer (see seam: audit-state-and-recovery).
must_preserve: The `okdctl destroy` flow which legitimately needs to remove these VMs.
